question:
Which of the following statement(s) is true?

A) Higher inflation means lower real GDP, ceteris paribus

B) Price Index is 200 if nominal GDP and real GDP are the same
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** higher inflation rate** indicates that the **general price level **of goods and services in an economy is **increasing**.
 
• This means that consumers will have to** pay more **for the same goods and services, resulting in a decrease in their purchasing power.
 
• As a result, businesses will produce less, leading to **lower real GDP.**
 
• This **relationship **between** inflation and real GDP** is known as the **Phillips Curve**, which suggests an inverse relationship between the two variables.
 
• However, it is important to note that this relationship holds only in the **short run**.
 
• In the **long run**, the **Phillips Curve** becomes **vertical**, indicating that there is **no tradeoff **between inflation and real GDP.
 
• **Higher inflation** does lead to **lower real GDP** in the short run, ceteris paribus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A country's **market value** of all the **finished goods and services **significant to a particular economic sector, are used to measure** inflation**.
 
• **Price indices**, which focus on the **costs of a variety of goods and services** significant to a particular economic sector, are used to measure inflation.
 
• A positive relationship between inflation and real GDP, is not supported by economic theory or empirical evidence.
 
• **Nominal GDP** and **real GDP** are not always equal.
 
• **Nominal GDP** is the total value of goods and services produced in an economy, measured at current prices, while **real GDP** adjusts for inflation and measures economic output in constant dollars.
